# WAKE v0.5.0

WAKE now adds a compact, cross-model memory layer in front of the detailed checkpoint.

## Highlights

- Adds `WAKE_MEMORY_CAPSULE_V1` at `memory-capsule.md`.
- Capsule is capped at 8 KiB and stores task state rather than chat chronology.
- Recovery reads `state.json` and the capsule before falling back to `checkpoint.md`.
- Capsule refresh is deterministic local file work and does not consume another model turn.
- Watcher automatically refreshes the capsule when checkpoint mtime changes.
- Adds quota-pressure levels at 80/90/95 percent and seals the latest capsule from 90 percent.
- Adds `memory-refresh` and `memory-status` commands.
- Pause, rearm, complete, and handoff launch refresh stale memory before changing state.
- Recovery probes Git worktree status before running status/diff, avoiding noisy fallback help output.
- Keeps the existing `cli_continuation_only` Desktop/CLI boundary.

## Why

A long Codex task should recover from a concise task-state serialization, not by replaying
or rewriting the entire historical conversation. The capsule is intentionally portable so
another AI can read the same state without needing the original chat.

## Validation

- Python compile checks.
- 20 unit tests covering capsule creation, 8 KiB cap, stale-checkpoint refresh,
  quota-pressure sealing, handoff ordering, pause refresh, retry logic, and existing
  job lifecycle.
- PowerShell parser checks and shell-script validation.
- Local install and real continuation E2E on Windows.
- The real E2E created a fresh Codex thread, observed an initial WebSocket timeout with
  HTTPS fallback, then read `state.json` and `memory-capsule.md` before any checkpoint
  fallback, produced `WAKE_CAPSULE_V05_OK\n`, verified all 20 bytes, refreshed the
  capsule, and marked the job `completed`.
- The E2E also exposed noisy Git commands in a non-worktree; v0.5.0 now probes the
  worktree first and skips status/diff when the probe fails.
